newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares mixed to firm in thin volumes.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares mixed to firm in thin volumes.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares were mixed to firmer in thin volumes on Monday with brokers saying trade was directionless and dull.

"The market was very dull and directionless, typical of a Monday. There has not been any exciting news lately to give direction to the market and it's also that time of the year when people start looking at the skies for rains," one broker said.
"There were a few gains here and there as well as a few losses but in very thin trading," he added.

The key industrial index rose 36.58 points to close at 6,841.10, boosted mainly by publishing group Zimpapers' 100-cent jump to 1,500, sugar refinery ZSR's 50-cent rise to 1,300, sugar producer Hippo's 40-cent gain to 800 and transport group Clan's 20-cent addition to 200.
Five-cent gains were recorded in conglomerate TA Holdings at 135, tyre manufacturer Dunlop at 175, battery manufacturer Chloride at 70 and tissue-mill KCI at 50.
However, food canning group Cairns dropped 30 cents to 800 while pork processor Colcom shed 10 cents to 290 and discount house DCZ eased five cents to 160.
Minings were mildly firmer with small buyers pushing gold producer Ashanti 500 cents higher to 14,000 while Wankie Colliery put on five cents to 350.
The mining index gained 37.75 points to end at 1,245.70.
